items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: I want you to go to Berklee and you should go to Berklee and study with Billy Pierce.

ctx.x: I was in McDonald’s All American Band, a high school all-American band, which takes two students — I don’t know if it exists anymore — but it takes two students from each state in the United States. I represented Colorado, me and another person, and Delfayo Marsalis represented Louisiana. Well when I met him, the first thing I said was, “I want to meet your brother.” We were in New York doing the Macy’s Day parade. And so I remember afterwards, and the first thing I go up to him and I said, “I want to play with…

Really interesting. And it makes me think about earlier you had said, referring to Art Blakey and Elvin Jones, when they passed that there was a short of a signal to shift in jazz some, but you found a mentor and hung with that guy and it led to what you were hoping for. I mean the mentorship thing is not what it used to be, at least in talking to these fellows from the thirties and the forties it seems like.
